654.name: Bytes
654.docs:
Limit the amount of memory that can be used for a single frame to this many bytes.

It may not be enforced precisely due to allocator overhead
and the decoder potentially allocating small auxiliary buffers,
but it will precisely limit the size of the output buffer for each frame.

427.name: DecoderNotFound

729.name: read_into_buffer
729.docs:
Reads the data of the current frame into a pre-allocated buffer.

`Self::next_frame_info` needs to be called beforehand.
The length of `buf` must be at least `Self::buffer_size`.
Deinterlaces the result.

175.name: top

350.name: get_mut

Gets a mutable reference to the writer instance used by this encoder.

500.name: FrameMetadata
500.docs:
Decoded all information of the next frame, except the image data.

The returned frame does **not** contain any owned image data.

Call `current_frame_mut()` to access the frame info.

223.name: EncodingFormatError
223.docs: The image has incorrect properties, making it impossible to encode as a gif.

575.name: Version

348.name: write_raw_extension
348.docs:
Writes a raw extension to the image.

This method can be used to write an unsupported extension to the file. `func` is the extension
identifier (e.g. `Extension::Application as u8`). `data` are the extension payload blocks. If any
contained slice has a lenght > 255 it is automatically divided into sub-blocks.

373.name: ColorOutput

171.name: delay
171.docs: Frame delay in units of 10 ms.

775.name: streaming_decoder
775.docs: Low-level, advanced decoder. Prefer [`Decoder`] instead, which can stream frames too.

498.name: SubBlock
498.docs:
Decoded a sub-block.

Call `last_ext_sub_block()` to get the sub-block data. It won't be available after this event.

221.name: MissingColorPalette
221.docs: The image has no color palette which is required.

321.name: new_control_ext
321.docs:
Constructor for control extension data.

`delay` is given in units of 10 ms.

346.name: write_frame
346.docs:
Writes a frame to the image.

Note: This function also writes a control extension if necessary.

371.name: RGBA
371.docs:
The decoder expands the image data to 32bit RGBA.
This affects:

 - The buffer buffer of the `Frame` returned by [`Decoder::read_next_frame`].
 - `Decoder::fill_buffer`, `Decoder::buffer_size` and `Decoder::line_length`.

144.name: from_u8
144.docs: Converts `u8` to a `Extension` if it is known.

194.name: make_lzw_pre_encoded
194.docs:
Replace frame's buffer with a LZW-compressed one for use with [`Encoder::write_lzw_pre_encoded_frame`].

Frames can be compressed in any order, separately from the `Encoder`, which can be used to compress frames in parallel.

496.name: ext
496.docs: An ext label of `0` is used when the sub block does not belong to an extension.

571.name: current_frame
571.docs: Current frame info as a ref.

344.name: new
344.docs:
Creates a new encoder.

`global_palette` gives the global color palette in the format `[r, g, b, ...]`,
if no global palette shall be used an empty slice may be supplied.

569.name: last_ext_sub_block
569.docs:
Data of the last extension sub block that has been decoded.
You need to concatenate all subblocks together to get the overall block content.

140.name: Text
140.docs:
Plain Text extension.

This instructs the decoder to render a text as characters in a grid of cells, in a
mono-spaced font of its choosing. This is seldom actually implemented and ignored by
ImageMagick. The color is always taken from the global table which further complicates any
use. No real information on the frame sequencing of this block is available in the
standard.

190.name: from_rgb
190.docs:
Creates a frame from pixels in RGB format.

This is a lossy method. In the `gif` format only 256 colors can appear in a single frame.
The palette will be reduced by the NeuQuant algorithm if necessary. Different frames have
independent palettes.

*Note: This method is not optimized for speed.*

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height * 3`.

492.name: BackgroundColor
492.docs: Index of the background color in the global palette.

567.name: update
567.docs:
Updates the internal state of the decoder.

Returns the number of bytes consumed from the input buffer
and the last decoding result.

188.name: from_palette_pixels
188.docs:
Creates a frame from a palette and indexed pixels.

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height`.
*   If the length of palette > `256 * 3`.

792.name: gif

565.name: StreamingDecoder
565.docs:
GIF decoder which emits [low-level events](Decoded) for items in the GIF file

To just get GIF frames, use [`crate::Decoder`] instead.

690.name: check_lzw_end_code
690.docs:
Configure if LZW encoded blocks must end with a marker end code.

The default is `false`.

When turned on, all image data blocks—which are LZW encoded—must contain a special bit
sequence signalling the end of the data. LZW processing terminates when this code is
encountered. The specification states that it must be the last code output by the encoder
for an image.

When turned off then image data blocks can simply end. Note that this might silently ignore
some bits of the last or second to last byte.

186.name: from_rgba_speed
186.docs:
Creates a frame from pixels in RGBA format.

`speed` is a value in the range [1, 30].
The higher the value the faster it runs at the cost of image quality.
A `speed` of 10 is a good compromise between speed and quality.

This is a lossy method. The `gif` format does not support arbitrary alpha but only a 1-bit
transparency mask per pixel. Any non-zero alpha value will be interpreted as a fully opaque
pixel. Additionally, only 256 colors can appear in a single frame. The palette will be
reduced by the NeuQuant algorithm if necessary. Different frames have independent palettes.

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height * 4`.
*   If `speed < 1` or `speed > 30`

34.name: into
34.docs: Calls `U::from(self)`. That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of [From]<T> for U chooses to do.

738.name: icc_profile
738.docs: ICC profile stored in the image.

686.name: check_frame_consistency
686.docs:
Configure if frames must be within the screen descriptor.

The default is `false`.

When turned on, all frame descriptors being read must fit within the screen descriptor or
otherwise an error is returned and the stream left in an unspecified state.

When turned off, frames may be arbitrarily larger or offset in relation to the screen. Many
other decoder libraries handle this in highly divergent ways. This moves all checks to the
caller, for example to emulate a specific style.

107.name: Extension
107.docs:
Known GIF extension labels.

These are extensions which may be interpreted by the library and to which a specification with
the internal data layout is known.

434.name: Format
434.docs: Returned if the image is found to be malformed.

761.name: DecoderIter
761.docs: Use `decoder.into_iter()` to iterate over the frames

182.name: buffer
182.docs:
Buffer containing the image data.
Only indices unless configured differently.

684.name: set_color_output
684.docs: Configure how color data is decoded.

105.name: AnyExtension
105.docs:
A newtype wrapper around an arbitrary extension ID.

An extension is some amount of byte data organized in sub-blocks so that one can skip over it
without knowing the semantics. Though technically you likely want to use a `Application`
extension, the library tries to stay flexible here.

This allows us to customize the set of impls compared to a raw `u8`. It also clarifies the
intent and gives some inherent methods for interoperability with known extension types.

432.name: LzwError
432.docs: Error encountered while decoding an LZW stream.

180.name: palette
180.docs: Frame local color palette if available.

507.name: Decoded
507.docs: Indicates whether a certain object has been decoded

532.name: decode_lzw_encoded_frame_into_buffer
532.docs:
Converts into the given buffer. It must be [`buffer_size()`] bytes large.

Pixels are always deinterlaced, so update `frame.interlaced` afterwards if you're putting the buffer back into the frame.

682.name: read_info
682.docs:
Reads the logical screen descriptor including the global color palette

Returns a [`Decoder`]. All decoder configuration has to be done beforehand.

732.name: line_length
732.docs: Line length of the current frame

505.name: LzwDataCopied
505.docs: Copied (or consumed and discarded) compressed data of the current frame. In bytes.

253.name: OutOfMemory
253.docs: Failed to internally allocate a buffer of sufficient size.

655.name: MemoryLimit
655.docs: The maximum amount of memory the decoder is allowed to use for each frame

76.name: Block
76.docs:
Known GIF block labels.

Note that the block uniquely specifies the layout of bytes that follow and how they are
framed. For example, the header always has a fixed length but is followed by a variable amount
of additional data. An image descriptor may be followed by a local color table depending on
information read in it. Therefore, it doesn't make sense to continue parsing after encountering
an unknown block as the semantics of following bytes are unclear.

The extension block provides a common framing for an arbitrary amount of application specific
data which may be ignored.

428.name: EndCodeNotFound
428.docs: Expected an end-code, but none found.

730.name: fill_buffer
730.docs:
Reads data of the current frame into a pre-allocated buffer until the buffer has been
filled completely.

The buffer length must be an even number of pixels (multiple of 4 if decoding RGBA).

`Self::next_frame_info` needs to be called beforehand. Returns `true` if the supplied
buffer could be filled completely. Should not be called after `false` had been returned.

176.name: left
176.docs: Offset from the left border of the canvas.

503.name: BytesDecoded
503.docs: Decoded some data of the current frame. Size is in bytes, always > 0

351.name: into_inner
351.docs: Finishes writing, and returns the `io::Write` instance used by this encoder

728.name: current_frame_info
728.docs:
Query information about the frame previously advanced with [`Self::next_frame_info`].

Returns `None` past the end of file.

174.name: needs_user_input
174.docs: True if the frame needs user input to be displayed.

349.name: get_ref
349.docs: Gets a reference to the writer instance used by this encoder.

651.name: Unlimited
651.docs:
Enforce no memory limit.

If you intend to process images from unknown origins this is a potentially dangerous
constant to use, as your program could be vulnerable to decompression bombs. That is,
malicious images crafted specifically to require an enormous amount of memory to process
while having a disproportionately small file size.

The risks for modern machines are a bit smaller as the size of each frame cannot
exceed 16GiB, but this is still a significant amount of memory.

726.name: new
726.docs: Create a new decoder with default options.

222.name: InvalidMinCodeSize
222.docs: LZW data is not valid for GIF. This may happen when wrong buffer is given to `write_lzw_pre_encoded_frame`

574.name: version
574.docs:
The version number of the GIF standard used in this image.

We suppose a minimum of `V87a` compatibility. This value will be reported until we have
read the version information in the magic header bytes.

347.name: write_extension
347.docs:
Writes an extension to the image.

It is normally not necessary to call this method manually.

372.name: Indexed
372.docs: The decoder returns the raw indexed data.

497.name: is_last
497.docs: if true, then no more sub-blocks are available in this block.

220.name: TooManyColors
220.docs: The image has too many colors.

345.name: set_repeat
345.docs: Write an extension block that signals a repeat behaviour.

143.name: Application
143.docs:
Application extension.

See [ImageMagick] for an idea of commonly recognized extensions.

[ImageMagick]: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b0b58c6303195928060f55f9c3ca8233ab7f7733/coders/gif.c#L1128

193.name: write_lzw_pre_encoded_frame
193.docs:
Writes a frame to the image, but expects `Frame.buffer` to contain LZW-encoded data
from [`Frame::make_lzw_pre_encoded`].

Note: This function also writes a control extension if necessary.

495.name: BlockStart
495.docs:
The start of a block.
`BlockStart(Block::Trailer)` is the very last decode event

570.name: current_frame_mut
570.docs: Current frame info as a mutable ref.

191.name: from_rgb_speed
191.docs:
Creates a frame from pixels in RGB format.

`speed` is a value in the range [1, 30].

This is a lossy method. In the `gif` format only 256 colors can appear in a single frame.
The palette will be reduced by the NeuQuant algorithm if necessary. Different frames have
independent palettes.

The higher the value the faster it runs at the cost of image quality.
A `speed` of 10 is a good compromise between speed and quality.

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height * 3`.
*   If `speed < 1` or `speed > 30`

493.name: HeaderEnd
493.docs:
Palette and optional `Application` extension have been parsed,
reached frame data.

189.name: from_indexed_pixels
189.docs:
Creates a frame from indexed pixels in the global palette.

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height`.

691.name: allow_unknown_blocks
691.docs:
Configure if unknown blocks are allowed to be decoded.

The default is `false`.

When turned on, the decoder will allow unknown blocks to be in the
`BlockStart` position.

When turned off, decoded block starts must mark an `Image`, `Extension`,
or `Trailer` block. Otherwise, the decoded image will return an error.
If an unknown block error is returned from decoding, enabling this
setting may allow for a further state of decoding on the next attempt.

This option also allows unknown extension blocks. The decoder assumes the follow the same
block layout, i.e. a sequence of zero-length terminated sub-blocks immediately follow the
extension introducer.

741.name: bg_color
741.docs:
Index of the background color in the global palette

In practice this is not used, and the background is
always transparent

187.name: from_grayscale_with_alpha
187.docs:
Creates a frame from pixels in LumaAlpha format (grayscale pixels with transparency).

This is a lossy method. The `gif` format does not support arbitrary alpha but only a 1-bit
transparency mask per pixel. Any non-zero alpha value will be interpreted as a fully opaque
pixel. The least used color will be used to indicate alpha and replace with the closest other color
in the image. Different frames have independent palettes.

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height * 2`.

564.name: Decoder
564.docs: GIF decoder. Create [`DecodeOptions`] to get started, and call [`DecodeOptions::read_info`].

689.name: skip_frame_decoding
689.docs:
Configure whether to skip decoding frames.

The default is false.

When turned on, LZW decoding is skipped. [`Decoder::read_next_frame`] will return
compressed LZW bytes in frame's data.
[`Decoder::next_frame_info`] will return the metadata of the next frame as usual.
This is useful to count frames without incurring the overhead of decoding.

739.name: into_inner
739.docs: Abort decoding and recover the `io::Read` instance

185.name: from_rgba
185.docs:
Creates a frame from pixels in RGBA format.

This is a lossy method. The `gif` format does not support arbitrary alpha but only a 1-bit
transparency mask per pixel. Any non-zero alpha value will be interpreted as a fully opaque
pixel. Additionally, only 256 colors can appear in a single frame. The palette will be
reduced by the NeuQuant algorithm if necessary. Different frames have independent palettes.

*Note: This method is not optimized for speed.*

# Panics:
*   If the length of pixels does not equal `width * height * 4`.

687.name: read_next_frame
687.docs:
Reads the next frame from the image.

Do not call `Self::next_frame_info` beforehand.
Deinterlaces the result.

You can also call `.into_iter()` on the decoder to use it as a regular iterator.

737.name: xmp_metadata
737.docs: XMP metadata stored in the image.

685.name: set_memory_limit
685.docs: Configure a memory limit for decoding.

106.name: into_known
106.docs: Decode the label as a known extension.

256.name: Format
256.docs: Returned if the to image is not encodable as a gif.

733.name: palette
733.docs: Returns the color palette relevant for the frame that has been decoded

179.name: interlaced
179.docs: True if the image is interlaced.

506.name: DataEnd
506.docs: No more data available the current frame.

531.name: decode_lzw_encoded_frame
531.docs:
Converts the frame in-place, replacing its LZW buffer with pixels.

If you get an error about invalid min code size, the buffer was probably pixels, not compressed data.

254.name: WriterNotFound
254.docs: Expected a writer but none found.

429.name: UnexpectedEof
429.docs: Decoding could not complete as the reader completed prematurely.

529.name: DecodeOptions
529.docs: Options for opening a GIF decoder. [`DecodeOptions::read_info`] will start the decoder.

252.name: FrameBufferTooSmallForDimensions
252.docs: Frame buffer is too small for the declared dimensions.
